 In The Court Of Sh. Abhishek Kumar
 Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate-01
 Patiala House Courts, New Delhi District:
 New Delhi
Cr Cases 8000/2019
Food Safety Officer Vs. Sh Rajeev Kumar Gupta.
 Judgment
(a) Serial number of the case : 8000-2019 (b) Name of the complainant : Food Safety Officer,
 Department of Food Safety,
 Govt of NCT of Delhi. 
(c) Name of the accused person : Rajeev Kumar Gupta s/o  Sh M.P. Gupta  M/s Gupta Kali Mirch Wala  Opp. Khasra No. 142/352,
 Extended Abadi Village  Kanjhawala, Delhi-81.
 R/o B-2/10, Phase-I, Budh  Vihar, Sultanpuri C Block  Delhi-86. 
(d) Offences charged of : U/s 51 and 59 (i) of FSS Act (e) Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty (f) Final Judgment : Accused stands acquitted.
(g) Date of institution of case : 11.09.2019 (h) Date of final arguments : 29.05.2024 (i) Date of Judgment : 30.05.2024 Cr. Case 8000-2019 FSO vs Rajeev Kumar Gupta Page No. 1 of 12  BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE 1. The present complaint has been filed by the Food Safety Department through Food Safety Officer under Section 26 of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act')
against the accused for the violation of the provision under section 26 (1) & 26 (2) (i) r/w section 3 (1) (zz) (v) & (vii) and Section 26 (2) (i) r/w section 3 (1) (zx) of the FSS Act r/w Regulation 2.9.15.1 of the Food Safety & Standards (Food Product & Additive) Regulations, 2011, punishable under section 59 (i) & 51 of the FSS Act, 2006. 
Pfa vs Rajeev Kumar Gupta on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90132873/
1 2. After the filing of the complaint, the examination of the complainant was dispensed with as the complaint was filed in the official capacity being a public servant. Thereafter, cognizance of the offences was taken and summons were issued to the accused. 
3. After the appearance of the accused, he was admitted to bail and copy of the complaint was supplied. Thereafter, notice was framed against the accused for the offence u/s 51 & 59 (i) of the FSS Act, 2006 to which the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 
4. Thereafter, prosecution evidence was recorded. During the prosecution evidence, the prosecution has examined four witnesses. The testimony of the witnesses in short is mentioned herein after. 
Cr. Case 8000-2019 FSO vs Rajeev Kumar Gupta Page No. 2 of 12 5. PW-1 FSO Tarun Negi has deposed that on 24/12/2018, he visited the shop in question along with FSO Saurabh Sharma, where the found the accused conducting the business in the premises and having stored Black Pepper for the same of human consumtion in sealed packets. Further, the Black Pepper was lying in open plastic bag bearing no label declaration. Thereafter, he expressed the intention to purchase the sample of Black Pepper and the accused agreed for the same but no public witness joined the sample proceedings and FSO Saurabh Sharma became the witness. 
5.1. Thereafter, at about 4PM, he purchased 2 KG of Black Pepper upon payment of Rs.810/- vide FBO receipt, which is Ex.PW1/A and put the Black Pepper in the plain and dried four plastic jars by mixing them properly with the help of Jhaba. Then, it was converted into four counterparts and all the samples counterparts were separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed as per the rules with the DO slips and DO stamps bearing signatures on the counterparts from top to bottam where the accused signed on the slips and wrappers.
5.2. Thereafter, he prepared the notice in Form No. V A, which is Ex.PW1/B and FBO/accused signed on the same against acknowledgement. Then, panchnama which is Ex.PW1/C was prepared and all the documents were read over to the accused in Cr. Case 8000-2019 FSO vs Rajeev Kumar Gupta Page No. 3 of 12 Hindi. Then, he prepared raid report, which is Ex.PW1/D and upon asking,
accused denied to send one counterpart to NABL Laboratory. 
5.3. Further, on 26.12.2018, he sent one counterpart to the Food Analyst vide letter, which is Ex.PW1/E and deposited the remaining counterparts with the DO. The receipt in this regard is Ex.PW1/F. Thereafter, report of the FA was received through DO, which is Ex.PW1/G and upon the directions of the Commissioner, investigation commenced. During the same, the DO sent the letter to the accused, which is Ex.PW1/H and one copy to him, which is Ex.PW1/H-1. He has also served a copy of the letter personally along with the copy of the report of the FA to the accused, who signed the copy, which is Ex.PW1/H-2 and Ex.PW1/H-3. Thereafter, letters were sent to the VAT office. 
After the conclusion of the investigation, the case file was put up before DO, who sought the consent from the Commissioner, which is Ex.PW1/K and filed the complaint, which is Ex.PW1/L.
Pfa vs Rajeev Kumar Gupta on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90132873/
2 6. PW-2 Saurabh Sharma has deposed on the same lines as PW-1. The witness was duly cross-examined by the accused. 
7. PW-3 DO Ranjit Singh has deposed that he has received the file from PW-1 and produced the same before the Commissioner for the grant of sanction, which was subsequently accorded. He identified the signature of the Commissioner. 
Cr. Case 8000-2019 FSO vs Rajeev Kumar Gupta Page No. 4 of 12 8. PW-4 S M Bhardwaj is the Food Analyst, who stated that he received the sample of black pepper on 26.12.2018 and issued the report on 04.01.2019. He found the sample to be unsafe as it was coated with mineral oil, which is prohibited as per the Regulations and sample to be sub-standard as the content of Volatile oil content was less than the prescribed limit of 2%. He further stated that he adopted the DGHS Manual to conduct the test and referred to his report, which is already Ex.PW1/G.
9. After the closure of the prosecution evidence, the statement of the accused was recorded and accused did not lead any defence evidence despite opportunity. Thereafter, final arguments were heard at length and matter was reserved for orders. Before proceeding ahead, it will be pertinent to refer to the provision of law involved in the present case. 
10. Section 51 of the Act provides punishment for the sale, storage, distribution and import of any food article for human consumption, which is sub-standard. The definition of substandard food is provided under section 3 (zx) of the Act, wherein it is mentioned that the food shall be deemed to be substandard if it does not meet the specified standards but not so as to render the article of food unsafe. The sample was found to be substandard on the basis of the report of FA as it was contravening the Regulations 2.9.15.1 of the Food Safety and Cr. Case 8000-2019 FSO vs Rajeev Kumar Gupta Page No. 5 of 12 Standards (Food Products and Additives) Regulations, 2011. As per the regulations, the sample must conform to certain standards wherein one of the standard ie mentioned at serial no. (viii), the volatile oil contents on dry basis should not be less than 2.0%
whereas in the present case, it was found to be 1.64%.
11. Section 59 of the Act provides for punishment for the manufacture, storage, sale, distribution and import of any article of food for human consumption, which is unsafe. The unsafe food has been defined u/s 3 (1) (zz) of the Act. There are various parameters mentioned under the said definition which makes the food unsafe and the categories for ready reference are mentioned as below:
(zz) unsafe food means an article of food whose nature, substance or quality is so affected as to render it injurious to health:--
(i) by the article itself, or its package thereof, which is composed, whether wholly or in part, of poisonous or deleterious substances; or Pfa vs Rajeev Kumar Gupta on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90132873/
3 (ii) by the article consisting, wholly or in part, of any filthy, putrid, rotten,
decomposed or diseased animal substance or vegetable substance; or (iii) by virtue of its unhygienic processing or the presence in that article of any harmful substance; or (iv) by the substitution of any inferior or cheaper substance whether wholly or in part; or (v) by addition of a substance directly or as an ingredient which is not permitted; or (vi) by the abstraction, wholly or in part, of any of its constituents; or (vii) by the article being so coloured, flavoured or coated, powdered or polished, as to damage or conceal the article or to make it appear better or of greater value than it really is;or (viii) by the presence of any colouring matter or preservatives other than that specified in respect thereof; or (ix) by the article having been infected or infested with worms, weevils, or insects; or (x) by virtue of its being prepared, packed or kept under insanitary conditions; or (xi) by virtue of its being mis-branded or sub-standard or food containing extraneous matter; or Cr. Case 8000-2019 FSO vs Rajeev Kumar Gupta Page No. 6 of 12 (xii) by virtue of containing pesticides and other contaminants in excess of quantities 12. Further, as per the regulation 2.9.15.1, the black pepper has to be free from added colour,
mineral oil and any other harmful substances. Thus, in the present case, the product was found unsafe as it was not free from mineral oil and in violation of Section 3 (i) (zz)
(v) for the addition of a substance directly which is not permitted and (viii), for the presence of colouring matter or preservatives. 
13. Now coming to the case in hand, the defence counsel has raised a very interesting position of law, wherein the above mentioned regulations stands amended by way of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products and Additives), Regulations 2020 which stood notified. The counsel has drawn the attention of the court to the substituted regulation 2.9.15.1, wherein the standard has been given for black, white and green pepper. He has stated that as per the regulation, now there is no prohibition for the use of mineral oil and the said word has been removed from the regulation. Further, as per the Regulation 3.4.1 regarding the processing aids, the use of white mineral oil as per the appendix C Pfa vs Rajeev Kumar Gupta on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90132873/
4 has been permitted for all the categories of food. He has also stated that as per the Amended Regulation, the volatile oil contents has been reduced from 2% to 1%, indicating that the content shall not be less than 1% now. He further submits that the benefit of Amended Regulation has to be given to the accused as the trial is pending and it will have retrospective effect on Cr. Case 8000-2019 FSO vs Rajeev Kumar Gupta Page No. 7 of 12 the trial. He has referred to certain judgments to support his contentions. 
13.1. The counsel has also submitted that the Food Analyst has not mentioned the method of analysis, which is the requirement of the law and during his cross-examination, he has stated that he has adopted the method as per DGHS Manual but the department has issued notification, notifying the methods to be adopted by the labs and the same is in contravention to the same. 
14. On the other hand, Ld SPP has submitted that the department has proved the case beyond reasonable doubt and benefit of the new Regulation cannot be extended to the accused as the sample was lifted prior to the Amendment. Further, there is no requirement to state the specific name of method adopted by the Analyst and he can refer to the DGHS Manual for the same. 
15. After going through the record and the submissions of the parties, no material contradiction is found in the testimony of the witnesses with respect to the lifting of sample and subsequent proceedings conducted. I am not in agreement with the submission of the counsel that the sanction is not proper as the Commissioner has used the word 'accorded my consent' and not the word sanction which is in violation of the provision of Law. As per my opinion, section 42 Cr. Case 8000-2019 FSO vs Rajeev Kumar Gupta Page No. 8 of 12 (4) does not state that the word sanction has to be used for the launching of the prosecution. Upon analysis of the sanction, it is found that the Commissioner had accorded the sanction for the institution of the prosecution by particularly refering to the section 42 (4) of the Act and the use of the word 'accorded my consent' will not nullify the sanction granted and the same will be proper as per the Law. 
16. As far as the submission of the counsel is concerned with respect to the Amendment of the Regulation in the year 2020, vide which use of mineral oil for processing is not a violation any more and also the content of volatile oil has been reduced to minimum 1% and its applicability to the present case, I am of the opinion that the counsel has rightly pointed out towards the position of law and any benefit of the same can be granted to the accused before the judgment. This argument of the counsel is duly supported by the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Municipal Corporation of Delhi vs M/s Hindustan Breakfast Food Manufacturing Factory and Ors (Crl R. No.
127/77) wherein accused was discharged from the prosecution as due to the subsequent Amendment, the standard of moisture in cornflex was enhanced to 7.5% and the case of the accused fell within the parameter on account of the amendment. Also, the case of Allahabad High Court in Shyam Lal vs State, AIR 1968 All. 392 was referred in the said case, wherein it was observed that the true rule of Cr. Case 8000-2019 FSO vs Rajeev Kumar Gupta Page No. 9 of 12 construction of a penal statute is that where the Legislature evinces its intention to modify the Law in favour of the accused, so as to reduce the rigour of the Law in the light of the past experience and changed social conditions so long as the prosecution of the accused has not concluded by a judgment of a conviction, the proceedings against him are regarded as inchoate and the Law applicable to him will Pfa vs Rajeev Kumar Gupta on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90132873/
5 be the Law as amended by the Legislature. It was also observed that the Court trying an accused has to take into consideration the Law as exists on the date of the judgment. 
17. In the light of the above judgments and the Amendment of the Regulations, it can be safely held that the sample lifted will not fall within the category of substandard food as the volatile oil content shall not be less than the prescribed limit of 1% as per the new Amendment and in the present case,
the report of the Food Analyst states the volatile oil content on dry basis to be 1.64%, which is more than the prescribed limit. 
18. Further, the use of the mineral oil is no more prohibited as per the Amended Regulations and thus, presence of the same in the black pepper will not make the food unsafe. 
Cr. Case 8000-2019 FSO vs Rajeev Kumar Gupta Page No. 10 of 12 19. It is also to be noted that as per the Act, a duty has been casted upon the laboratory conducting the analysis of the sample, to state the method of analysis and mere mentioning of DGHS Manual without specifying the name of the method will not be in consonance to the rules and regulations of the Act. Furthermore, it has come in the testimony of PW-4, who is the Food Analyst in the present case that he is aware about the methods prescribed in the FASSI Manual which replaces the DGHS Manual and he has specifically stated that the methods prescribed in DGHS Manual are still valid and the same methods have been mentioned in the FASSI Manual. Thus, the testimony of the witness is self explanatory that he has not followed the methods of the FASSI Manual and it is to be remembered that the notifications issued by the FASSI are not an empty formality and all the rules have to be followed in letter and spirit by the labs conducting the test and they cannot justify the report simply on the grounds that the old methods are still valid without mentioning the name of the test. 
20. In nutshell, I am of the considered opinion that no case is made out against the accused in the light of the Amendment to the Food Safety & Standards (Food Products and Additives), 2020 and as discussed above, the sample of the black pepper is found to be conforming to the standards prescribed in the Amendment and the benefit of the same will be extended to the accused in the present case. Also, if the Amendment is not considered, still the case of the Cr. Case 8000-2019 FSO vs Rajeev Kumar Gupta Page No. 11 of 12 prosecution will fail as the essential requirements to state the method of analysis is missing in the report of the Food Analyst and the same makes the report doubtful. It is the fundmental right of the accused to know the name of the test applied for analysing the sample, in order to defend himself in the trial and any discrepancy to the said effect will make the report ineffective and non reliable. 
21. On account of the discussion as held above, the accused Rajeev Kumar Gupta s/o Shri M P Gupta stands acquitted for the offence u/s 51 and 59 (i) of the FSS Act, 2006. Accused is directed to furnish bail bonds in the sum of Rs.10,000/- u/s 437A Cr.P.C.
Announced in the open Court on 30th May, 2024 This judgment contains twelve pages and each page is signed by me.
